item.content:encoded:
MobiKwik Turns It Around

MobiKwik minted its highest-ever quarterly profit in Q2 FY27. The record performance came on the back of its financial services business delivering healthy revenue growth, while a tight leash on expenses helped the fintech company improve margins. 

Here’s a quick glance at MobiKwik’s Q2 FY27 numbers: 

  • Net profit of ₹11.8 Cr compared to a net loss of ₹28.6 Cr in Q2 FY26
  • Operating revenue rose 9.4% YoY to ₹295.7 Cr 
  • Total expenses declined a marginal 1.8% YoY to ₹290.9 Cr
  • EBITDA profit stood at ₹22.7 Cr against an EBITDA loss of ₹6.4 Cr in the year ago quarter

Lending Grabs The Spotlight: MobiKwik’s financial services business picked up in a big way in Q2 as the company disbursed a lot more loans and partnered with more lending partners during the quarter. At the same time, better loan book quality helped reduce expenses and improved the vertical’s gross profit. 

Payments’ Mixed Show: Although MobiKwik’s payments business processed much higher GMV in Q2 on a YoY basis, revenue barely grew. This is because the transaction mix skewed heavily towards payments that generate lower revenue. While this helped bring down payments gateway costs, the business’ take rate took a major hit.

Unlocking Operating Leverage: The quarter also saw both of MobiKwik’s core businesses expand their contribution margins, which helped offset the increased fixed expenses. Going forward, the company sees growing AI adoption in lending, engineering, customer experience, and risk management to further improve operating leverage and efficiency.

As the listed fintech company looks for a way to translate higher transactions into more revenue, here is a closer look at MobiKwik’s Q2 FY27 results…

From The Editor’s Desk

Pixxel CEO Clears Air On US Foray

  • Cofounder and CEO Awais Ahmed has clarified that the spacetech startup remains Indian-owned, managed and controlled amid criticism over the launch of its US subsidiary, Pixxel Federal.
  • The clarification comes after fellow spacetech startup GalaxEye highlighted its decision to operate through a single Indian entity, indirectly questioning the practice of setting up multiple entities across jurisdictions.
  • Pixxel launched Pixxel Federal to pursue US government contracts across civilian, defence and intelligence agencies. The startup, which has raised around $195 Mn to date, also plans to go public in India in the coming years.

Fireside Ventures’ Cofounder Quits

  • Cofounder and partner Vinay Singh is stepping down from the venture capital giant after nearly a decade-long stint. The investment firm is yet to announce his successor.
  • Singh now plans to “explore” the agentic commerce space and its implications for the future of consumption.
  • In his decade-long tenure, Singh grew the firm into a major consumer-focused VC firm. It has so far backed more than 65 Indian startups and manages assets of around $650 Mn across four funds.

ESDS’ Q2 Profit Surge

  • The AI company reported a 40.7% YoY jump in consolidated net profit to ₹31.1 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue surged 48% to ₹138.3 Cr.
  • The company’s EBITDA rose 18.3% YoY to ₹57.8 Cr, even as its EBITDA margin narrowed to 41.8% from 52% a year ago. Total expenses increased 63.7% to ₹103.5 Cr.
  • ESDS secured a $1.25 Bn AI cloud infrastructure deal with an Australia-based neocloud provider, with revenue expected from Q3 FY27. The company is also expanding its AI infrastructure capabilities through GPU clusters and its SWARAJ Cloud platform.

Record October For UPI

  • UPI transaction volume rose 5.8% MoM to a record 25.47 Bn in October, while transaction value increased 7.4% to ₹31.53 Lakh Cr, according to NPCI data.
  • October marked the first time UPI transactions crossed 25 Bn in volume and ₹30 Lakh Cr in value, driven partly by festive-season spending. On a YoY basis, transaction volume grew 23%, while value rose 16%.
  • The record growth comes ahead of the proposed rollout of MDR charges on select UPI payments above ₹2,000. NPCI deferred the implementation until after Diwali, with a revised date yet to be announced.

Pronto Founder’s Physical AI Bet

  • Pronto founder Anjali Sardana’s physical AI venture Provision Labs has acquired Mumbai-based hardware startup Basilisk for an undisclosed sum. As part of the deal, Basilisk founder Shourya Watwani will join Provision and lead its hardware efforts.
  • Founded in 2023, Basilisk is focused on perception technologies, which help machines interpret their surroundings. The startup claims to have developed a 3D hand-tracking model and built the first version of a tactile glove to capture touch-related data. 
  • This comes as Sardana recently launched Provision Labs to collect data for training and testing physical AI systems. The startup has also ramped up hiring of engineering and research teams across San Francisco, Toronto, and Bengaluru.

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

How Indrajaal Is Building India’s Shield Against Hostile Drones

As drones become cheaper and autonomous, defending borders and critical infrastructure against them is becoming more and more harder. To fix this gap, Indrajaal is building an integrated AI platform to detect, identify and neutralise hostile drones in real time.

Eyes In The Skies: Founded in 2024, Indrajaal is building a counter-drone ecosystem to secure India’s airspace. Its SkyOS platform brings together radars, radio-frequency sensors, cameras and AI to identify aerial threats and execute responses. It also offers a mobile counter-drone vehicle (Ranger), a spoofer called Repulsor and SkyCop, an interceptor drone.

Hunting Hostile Drones: Indrajaal claims that its systems are deployed at installations belonging to the Indian Army, Indian Navy and agencies under the Ministry of Home Affairs. On the back of this, the startup closed FY26 with a revenue of ₹100 Cr and is targeting a top line of ₹300 Cr in FY27. 

The Road Ahead: Indrajaal now plans to raise ₹420 Cr in a Series A round in the near term to expand manufacturing, R&D and its footprint in the Middle East and Europe. The startup also wants to build an autonomous airspace ecosystem for aerial transport. item.title: PowerUp Money Raises $10 Mn To Expand Wealth Management Services
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup PowerUp Money has raised $10 Mn (₹95 Cr) in a fresh funding round led by Flourish Ventures,…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup PowerUp Money has raised $10 Mn (₹95 Cr) in a fresh funding round led by Flourish Ventures, with participation from existing investors Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capital, 8i Ventures and DeVC. 

The startup plans to use the capital to expand its AI-led wealth management offerings, scale its managed advisory business and develop personalised financial planning solutions for Indian investors.

“We started by making high-quality investment advice accessible to every Indian. Today, AI makes it possible to deliver a much more comprehensive, wealth-manager-like experience digitally and at a fraction of traditional costs. A significant portion of this investment will go towards building an AI-powered wealth manager that brings personalised financial planning and ongoing portfolio guidance to every Indian,” PowerUp’s founder and CEO Prateek Jindal said. 

Jindal, who has also cofounded fintech major Uni Cards, launched PowerUp in 2025 to help customers manage their mutual fund portfolios. It claims to have over 15 Lakh customers, who track mutual fund portfolios worth over ₹2.5 Lakh Cr on its platform. Its mutual fund advisory subscription, PowerUp Elite, has over 1 Lakh paid members. 

Beyond mutual funds, the startup is now looking to combine investment advice, managed wealth services and digital advisory, becoming a full-stack financial planning platform in essence. 

The first step towards its new avatar has now come with the launch of its end-to-end digital wealth advisory offering, Elite Prime. The service includes an AI wealth coach and personal assistant, considers users’ financial goals, risk profiles and existing portfolios while helping them manage their portfolios and supporting their investment decisions. 

It is also seeking to scale up its managed wealth advisory offering, Infinite, to a broader customer base. 

Aimed at investors seeking more hands-on financial support, Infinite combines personalised financial planning, portfolio construction, multi-asset allocation, goal-based strategies, ongoing portfolio management and dedicated adviser support.

PowerUp claims that Infinite has scaled to nearly ₹500 Cr in assets under management (AUM) within around nine months of launch.

item.title: Clinics On Cloud Bags ₹120 Cr To Take Its Health ATMs Global
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Health tech startup Clinics On Cloud has raised ₹120 Cr (around $12.5 Mn) in its Series A funding round from…
item.content:encoded:
Health tech startup Clinics On Cloud has raised ₹120 Cr (around $12.5 Mn) in its Series A funding round from Model42, the medtech-focused investment arm of UAE-based backer Enlightened Minds Investments.

The Pune-based startup raised the fresh funds at a valuation of ₹600 Cr ($63.3 Mn)

In a statement, the startup said that it plans to utilise the fresh capital to bolster its AI-led healthcare capabilities, expand research and development (R&D), and accelerate the growth of its micro-clinic ecosystem. 

A chunk of the funding will also be used to strengthen its manufacturing capacity, scale strategic partnerships with healthcare providers and expand global footprint. 

“For eight years, we have built Clinics On Cloud with a simple belief that quality healthcare should never depend on someone’s pincode. This investment gives us the opportunity to take that vision global…,” said Clinics On Cloud cofounder and CEO Abhay Agarwal.

Founded in 2018 by Abhay and Manashrri Agarwal, Clinics On Cloud manufactures and deploys AI-powered “health ATMs”, portable box clinics and mobile medical units that deliver point-of-care preventive health checkups and telemedicine consultations. These solutions enable hospitals and government agencies to set up temporary micro-clinics.

It claims to have so far seen more than 3,500 deployments across 200 cities in India and seven other countries. Having screened more than 1.2 Cr patients so far, the startup claims to cater to the Indian Army, Navy and the Border Security Force (BSF).

The Pune-based startup now plans to position UAE as its global expansion hub, with an eye on exploring new markets across Africa, the US and Southeast Asia.

The fundraise comes amid growing investor interest in the healthtech sector, which is seeing renewed funding activity on the back of AI adoption. In September this year, smart ring maker Ultrahuman raised $70 Mn to fuel its integrated healthtech playbook.

In July, another AI-powered healthtech startup CARPL.ai also bagged $10 Mn in its Series A funding round led by International Finance Corporation (IFC). In the same month, actor Kunal Kapoor banded together with crowdfunding platform Ketto’s cofounders Varun Sheth and Zaheer Adenwala to launch healthtech startup MetaGO. 

At the heart of all this is the homegrown healthtech market, which is projected to become a $37 Bn opportunity by 2030.

item.title: Fireside Ventures’ Cofounder & Partner Vinay Singh To Step Down
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Fireside Ventures’ cofounder and partner Vinay Singh is stepping down from the investment firm after a nearly decade-long stint. In…
item.content:encoded:
Fireside Ventures’ cofounder and partner Vinay Singh is stepping down from the investment firm after a nearly decade-long stint.

In a statement, the venture capital (VC) firm said that Singh would “transition out of the firm”. The consumer-focused fund has so far not named his successor.

On his future course of action, Singh said that he now plans to explore the “frontiers of agentic commerce and its implications for the future of consumption”.

“… As AI reshapes commerce faster than most of us expected, I want to spend more time exploring the frontiers of agentic commerce and its implications for the future of consumption. I am excited for this next chapter, and deeply grateful to the Fireside family, and to every founder and LP (limited partner) who trusted us on this journey,” said Singh.

An alumnus of IIM Bangalore, Singh counts nearly two decades of experience under his belt. He previously worked at companies like Hindustan Unilever and Bankbazaar. He earlier also cofounded car servicing platform Stepni, which was later acquired by Quikr.

He eventually cofounded Fireside Ventures alongside Kanwaljit Singh, Kannan Sitaram and Dipanjan Basu in 2017. Over the past decade, the VC firm has emerged as one of India’s biggest consumer-focused venture funds and counts more than 65 startups in its portfolio. 

It currently claims to oversee more than $650 Mn in assets under management across four funds. The VC firm last closed its fourth fund at about $253 Mn in December last year. The investment firm currently claims to be helmed by a team of 12 principals and vice presidents.

The development comes as a host of seasoned fund managers depart major VC firms to set up their own funds. Earlier this year, Ashish Agrawal, Ishaan Mittal and Tejeshwi Sharma quit Peak XV Partners to establish their own fund, Mettle Capital. 

Private equity (PE) firm L Catterton’s partner and co-head of India investments, Anjana Sasidharan, also stepped down from the company in March this year to set up Asthrum Capital. Another former Peak XV trio, comprising Shailesh Lakhani, Harshjit Sethi and Mayank Porwal, has launched Ambition Capital and is looking to raise $250 Mn for the maiden fund.

item.title: ideaForge Returns To Profitability In Q2, Reports Net Profit Of ₹6.5 Cr
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Dronetech major ideaForge posted a net profit of ₹6.5 Cr in the September quarter (Q2) of FY27. The company reported…
item.content:encoded:
Dronetech major ideaForge posted a net profit of ₹6.5 Cr in the September quarter (Q2) of FY27. The company reported a profit in the fiscal year FY26 before dipping back into the red in Q1, reporting a loss of ₹2.6 Cr. It had reported a loss of ₹19.6 Cr in the year-ago quarter.

ideaForge’s operating revenue grew 124% YoY to ₹91.3 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹40.8 Cr in the year-ago period. Sequentially, it rose by about 33% from ₹68.6 Cr in the preceding quarter.

Defence business, which includes UAV platforms and related solutions for military and security applications, accounted for 72% of Q2 FY27 revenue, while civil applications, catering to commercial, industrial and government applications outside defence, contributed 28%.

Including other income of ₹6.3 Cr, the company’s total income for the period stood at ₹97.6 Cr. 

Meanwhile, total expenses surged 41.9% YoY to ₹90.1 Cr. At ₹48.1 Cr, the cost of materials consumed to manufacture the drones constituted more than half of the total expenditure for the quarter. 

The company turned EBITDA positive during the quarter, reporting an EBITDA profit of ₹23.2 Cr against an EBITDA loss of ₹8 Cr in the year-ago quarter. EBITDA margin improved to 25.4% from negative 19.6% in Q2 FY26.

ideaForge said that it entered FY27 with an order book of more than ₹300 Cr, of which 50% was executed in the first half of the fiscal.

“As we enter the second half of FY27, our immediate priority is to sustain the pace of execution while bringing our new platforms closer to commercialisation. The combination of an expanding product portfolio, stronger indigenous technology capabilities and growing procurement opportunities gives us confidence in the road ahead,” ideaForge CEO Ankit Mehta said. 

Besides the financial disclosures for the quarter, the company also said that it has secured an investment of  ₹151 Cr from the Technology Development Board (TDB) via the RDI Fund to develop YETI, its logistics unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The UAV is being developed for applications such as cargo transportation, medical evacuation and personnel deployment, and can carry payloads of up to 200 kg.

Shares of ideaForge ended today’s trading session 1.75% higher at ₹639.70 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop Narrows Q2 Loss By 13% To ₹68.3 Cr, Revenue Up 31%
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Pernia’s Pop Up Shop parent Purple Style Labs (PSL) narrowed its consolidated net loss for the September quarter by 12.9%…
item.content:encoded:
Pernia’s Pop Up Shop parent Purple Style Labs (PSL) narrowed its consolidated net loss for the September quarter by 12.9% YoY to ₹68.3 Cr from ₹78.4 Cr loss incurred in the year-ago period. Sequentially, net loss went down by 22.5% from ₹88.1 Cr. 

Operating revenue for the quarter grew 30.7% YoY to ₹142.1 Cr from ₹108.7 Cr, and 19% QoQ from ₹119.4 Cr. Including other income of ₹3.9 Cr, it recorded a total income of ₹146 Cr during the quarter. 

The company reported an exceptional expense of ₹3.1 Cr during the quarter, resulting in a loss before tax of ₹69.3 Cr. 

“Exceptional item pertains to employee compensation expenses towards grant of employee stock options to eligible employees of the group and expense incurred towards fees paid for increase in authorised capital of subsidiary,” the company’s profit read.

Total expenses jumped 36.9% to ₹211.2 Cr from ₹154.3 Cr in the year-ago period. Purchases of stock in trade, at ₹118.4 Cr, was its biggest expense. 

The company’s EBITDA for Q2 FY27 amounted to ₹4 Cr, compared to breaking even in Q2 FY26. In the previous quarter, it had reported an EBITDA loss of ₹11 Cr. 

Founded in 2015 by Abhishek Agarwal, the company claims to sell luxury fashion apparel sourced from over 1,100 active designer brands. 

Its portfolio spans womenswear, menswear, jewellery, accessories and kidswear. It follows an omnichannel model combining ecommerce and 14 multi-designer retail stores across India. 

PSL, which operates the multi-brand luxury omnichannel fashion platform Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop, had listed on the bourses in September. Its ₹680 Cr IPO, comprising a fresh issue of shares with no OFS component, was oversubscribed at 1.29X. 

In terms of operational metrics, PSL reported a total GMV of ₹204 Cr in the quarter, with an average order value of ₹82,000. 

The stock closed today’s session 1.46% lower at ₹493.70 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: TBO Tek Q2 Profit Rises 12.5% YoY To ₹76 Cr, Revenue Up 53%
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Travel distribution platform TBO Tek reported a 12.5% year-on-year (YoY) increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹76 Cr for…
item.content:encoded:
Travel distribution platform TBO Tek reported a 12.5% year-on-year (YoY) increase in its consolidated net profit to ₹76 Cr for the September quarter of FY27 (Q2 FY27) from ₹67.6 Cr in the year-ago period. Operating revenue rose 52.6% YoY to ₹865.6 Cr.

On a sequential basis, the company’s performance was more muted. Its operating revenue fell 6.5% from ₹925.8 Cr recorded in the June quarter, while net profit fell 8.8% from ₹83.4 Cr.

Including other income of ₹14.8 Cr, total income for the quarter stood at ₹880.4 Cr.

On the other hand, total expenses jumped almost 54.8% to ₹780.7 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹504.5 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. Service fees, the largest expense item, surged49.2% to ₹304.6 Cr, while employee benefits expenses increased 76.8% to ₹190.7 Cr.

TBO Tek reported an exceptional expense of ₹8.14 Cr during the quarter, relating to suspected collusion involving current and former employees of its overseas subsidiary and the holding company.

Based on a preliminary assessment, the company estimated a net financial loss of ₹8.14 Cr and said it had initiated legal action and the process for an insurance claim. The final loss may change after the detailed assessment.

Further, tax expense for the quarter increased 46% YoY to ₹15.5 Cr.  Consequently, profit before tax stood at ₹91.5 Cr, against ₹78.2 Cr in Q2 FY26.

Profit before tax, after accounting for exceptional items, stood at ₹91.5 Cr, up 17% from ₹78.2 Cr in Q2 FY26. 

Beyond its financial performance, TBO Tek reported growth across its travel distribution business, with gross transaction value (GTV) rising 31% YoY during the quarter. Its hotels and ancillary business remained the larger contributor, while the airline segment also recorded growth.

The company said the quarter saw broad-based growth across India, Asia-Pacific (APAC), Europe and North America, alongside a recovery in its Middle East business despite geopolitical disruptions and higher fuel prices. It attributed the improvement in the region to potential market share gains, driven by service differentiation and reliability.

In India, both the airline and hotels and ancillary segments recorded growth. The company also reported an increase in monthly transacting buyers (MTBs), with its organic international business seeing a record number of active buyers during the quarter. TBO Tek attributed this to the benefits of its investments in key account management (KAM) hiring made last year.

Commenting on the performance, cofounder and joint managing director Ankush Nijhawan said the platform’s globally diversified source and destination market. Besides, TBO’s India-focused cost base also helped it navigate “macroeconomic headwinds”. He added that its customer relationships and service quality would remain key differentiators as the platform scales.

“Our organic adjusted EBITDA growth continues to outpace the gross profit growth for the second quarter in a row, demonstrating the platform’s structural operating leverage as earlier commercial investments drive greater platform activity without a proportionate increase in costs. These results reinforce our strategy of expanding distribution while using technology to improve productivity and lower our cost to serve,” cofounder and joint MD Gaurav Bhatnagar said.

Shares of TBO Tek ended today’s trading session 3.54% higher at ₹1591.25 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: ESDS Q2 Profit Zooms 41% YoY To ₹31.1 Cr, Revenue Up 48%
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Enterprise cloud and AI company ESDS Software Solution reported a 40.7% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit to ₹31.1…
item.content:encoded:
Enterprise cloud and AI company ESDS Software Solution reported a 40.7% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit to ₹31.1 Cr in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹22.1 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year.

Operating revenue rose 48% YoY to ₹138.3 Cr during the quarter. Sequentially, revenue increased 4% from ₹133 Cr in Q1 FY27, while net profit grew 6.2% from ₹29.3 Cr.

The company’s EBITDA increased 18.3% YoY and 3.1% sequentially to ₹57.8 Cr. However, its EBITDA margin contracted to 41.8% from 52% in Q2 FY26. The company’s profit after tax (PAT) margin stood at 22.5%.

The startup in a statement said it incurred ₹2.34 Cr in IPO-related marketing and advertising expenses during Q2 FY27. Excluding this expenditure, its EBITDA would have stood at ₹60.1 Cr, while profit before tax (PBT) would have been ₹42.47 Cr.

Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) contributed 50.5% of ESDS’ revenue in Q2 FY27, followed by managed services at 31.2% and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) at 18.3%. Existing customers accounted for 86.7% of the company’s revenue during the quarter.

“We delivered a strong performance in Q2 FY27, with revenue from operations growing 48% YoY and profit after tax increasing 40.7%,” said chairman and MD Piyush Somani.

He said AI infrastructure is entering a long-term global expansion cycle, with India still at an early stage of the opportunity. ESDS’ investment priorities, he added, are centred on AI factories, large-scale GPU clusters and its SWARAJ Cloud platform.

Meanwhile, chief financial officer (CFO) Nadukuru Sita Ramaiah said the company’s revenue streams across IaaS, managed services and SaaS provide “a foundation for long-term business stability”. He added that the focus remains on “maintaining healthy margins, optimising costs and strengthening cash flow management.”

In a business development, ESDS said that it entered in a $1.250 Bn AI cloud infrastructure deal with an unnamed Australia-based neocloud provider during the quarter. The agreement covers a cluster of 8,208 NVIDIA B300 GPUs for five years, with an extension option of two years.

The company expects revenue from the deal to begin in Q3 FY27. Its subsidiary SPOCHUB has received an advance of about ₹1,177 Cr from an overseas enterprise customer for a new GPUaaS project.

During the period, ESDS launched SWARAJ Cloud, an AI-autonomous sovereign cloud platform with 52+ integrated services. It also added SWARAJ Nandi (privileged access management), SWARAJ Hansa (AI-powered SIEM) and SWARAJ Sethu (DevSecOps) to its product suite, and appointed Sushil Kadu as Chief Product Officer.

Founded in 2005, Nashik-based ESDS provides cloud computing, data centre, managed services and AI-led digital solutions to government and enterprise customers. As of March 2026, the company claimed to serve more than 2,500 clients, including over 170 banking entities and 100 government organisations.

ESDS has utilised only ₹46.9 Cr of the ₹720 Cr raised through its IPO. Of the amount utilised, ₹38.2 Cr went towards issue expenses, while ₹8.8 Cr was spent on general corporate purposes.

The company has yet to utilise any portion of the ₹576 Cr earmarked for cloud and data centre equipment. The unspent IPO proceeds of ₹673 Cr are currently parked in fixed deposits.

The increase in other income, if reflected in the company’s financial statements, could potentially be partly attributable to interest earned on these deposits. However, ESDS has not explicitly attributed the increase to its fixed-deposit holdings.

ESDS’ Q2 Expenses

Meanwhile, ESDS’ total expenses increased 63.7% YoY and 4.8% sequentially to ₹103.5 Cr. The increase was largely driven by a sharp rise in other expenses, which accounted for nearly 49% of the total expenditure.

Employee benefit expenses rose 10.4% YoY and 18.4% sequentially to ₹29.8 Cr. Finance costs increased 18.4% YoY to ₹3.33 Cr, while depreciation and amortisation expenses grew 26.9% to ₹19.61 Cr.

Other expenses surged 182.3% YoY to ₹50.78 Cr from ₹17.99 Cr in Q2 FY26. However, they declined 3.3% sequentially from ₹52.5 Cr in Q1 FY27.

ESDS’ tax expense declined 17.2% YoY to ₹9 Cr from ₹10.9 Cr in the year-ago quarter. On a sequential basis, it increased 25.6% from ₹7.2 Cr.

Shares of ESDS ended today’s trading session 2.5% lower at ₹1,131.65 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: PB Fintech’s Shares Hit Fresh Low Of ₹928.1, Down 48% Since IRDAI’s Proposed Insurance Overhaul
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Shares of insurtech major PB Fintech hit a fresh 52-week low today, plunging about 8% to ₹926 apiece on the…
item.content:encoded:
Shares of insurtech major PB Fintech hit a fresh 52-week low today, plunging about 8% to ₹926 apiece on the BSE. The stock closed the day’s trading session 7.19% lower at ₹928.10 apiece on the BSE.

The company’s stock is down 48% since September 23, since the IRDAI floated its consultation paper to overhaul the insurance distribution industry

Its market capitalisation stood at ₹42,948.08 Cr ($4.53 Bn). PB Fintech commanded a market cap of $9.07 Bn at the end of the first week of September, over twice of its market cap now.

The dip today comes after the company’s quarterly disclosures last Friday. PB Fintech’s consolidated net profit rose 42.5% YoY to ₹192.4 Cr in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹135 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, profit increased 18% from ₹163 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Operating revenue grew nearly 35% YoY to ₹2,177.7 Cr, from ₹1,613.6 Cr in Q2 FY26. It rose 15% sequentially from ₹1,888.3 Cr in the June quarter. While total income stood at ₹2,277.6 Cr, total expenses increased 32.6% YoY to ₹2,067.7 Cr.

The company’s core online business, which includes Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, generated ₹1,336 Cr in revenue, up 39.5% YoY. Revenue from new initiatives rose 28% YoY to ₹842 Cr. Adjusted EBITDA increased 39% to ₹216 Cr, while adjusted EBITDA margin remained flat YoY at 10%

Brokerages have given mixed outlooks for the stock post the disclosures. HSBC and Dolat Capital retained their ‘Hold’ and ‘Reduce’ ratings, respectively, while Bernstein maintained its ‘Outperform’ call. 

HSBC kept its target price at ₹1,100 but cut its FY27-29 earnings per share (EPS) estimates by 2-4%, citing higher operating costs and regulatory uncertainty. Bernstein retained its target price of ₹1,085, citing 38% YoY growth in consolidated premiums and 22% growth in core credit disbursements.

Dolat Capital retained its ‘Reduce’ rating but cut its target price to ₹1,090 from ₹1,150. The brokerage said Q2 revenue rose 35% YoY to ₹2,177.7 Cr but was 4.2% below its estimate. EBIT also missed estimates by 32.7%, mainly due to higher advertising and other expenses.

It flagged concerns that proposed IRDAI rules could reduce insurance distribution payouts and affect PB Fintech’s PoSP model. Dolat cut its FY27-FY29 EPS estimates by 3%, 3.9% and 4.1%, respectively, due to uncertainty over the impact of the proposed rules.

PB Fintech’s Future Outlook

PB Fintech has said its PoSP insurance distribution business may need to be restructured if the IRDAI’s proposed rules are adopted in their current form.

During the earnings call, chairman and CEO Yashish Dahiya said the proposals could limit the scope of the existing PoSP model. The company will wait for the final regulations before deciding on its next steps.

Dahiya said PB Fintech was in informal discussions with the regulator about other options, which it would announce only after receiving certain regulatory approval. He added that the proposals could open up opportunities to offer non-insurance services, including potentially charging for claims support that Policybazaar currently provides for free, subject to the final rules.

PB Fintech has begun reducing costs, with hiring in October at a “very, very small fraction” of earlier levels, the management said. The company also plans to move existing executives into newer businesses and use AI to improve efficiency. Advertising and promotion expenses rose 59% YoY to ₹447 Cr in Q2, outpacing revenue growth.

Core credit disbursements rose 22% YoY to ₹2,791 Cr but were broadly flat sequentially. Management said it had focused on adding lending partners before pursuing further growth.

Bengaluru-based spacetech soonicorn Pixxel’s founder and CEO Awais Ahmed has dismissed questions over the startup’s Indian ownership and control following online criticism over the launch of its US subsidiary, Pixxel Federal.

In a post on X, Ahmed said Pixxel remains headquartered, owned, managed, and controlled in India, rejecting allegations questioning its corporate structure and national credentials.

“First, Pixxel is Indian-HQed, Indian owned, Indian-managed and Indian-controlled,” he said, adding that its primary Indian entity was incorporated in 2018, before any of its international entities.

Ahmed said the Indian entity is not a subsidiary of a US company and remains the primary vehicle for executing Pixxel’s Indian government, space, and defence programmes. Pixxel Federal’s board and CEO would have authority only over the US subsidiary and its operations, with no control over the startup’s Indian government programmes or domestic business, he added.

The clarification follows Pixxel’s announcement that it had established Pixxel Federal to pursue US government contracts across civilian, defence, and intelligence agencies.

Pixxel’s Ownership Structure

Ahmed said Pixxel has faced targeted social media attacks, anonymous emails to government customers, and attempts to cast doubt on its ownership, technology, and credentials.

Addressing its shareholding, he said Indian investors, including the founders, collectively hold the largest share by percentage, followed by investors from Singapore, the UK, and the US. No international investor has unilateral control over Pixxel beyond customary investor protections, he added.

Ahmed also said intellectual property developed for Indian government projects remains under Indian ownership and control, with these programmes executed through Indian entities and governed by Indian laws.

He said Pixxel’s overseas presence predates Pixxel Federal, with its existing US entity incorporated a few months after the Indian company in 2018 to serve American and international customers. Pixxel plans to set up entities in more countries as it expands globally.

“We intend to build a global space company rooted in Indian engineering. That means selling Indian technology worldwide, hiring internationally, establishing local entities where required, and complying with each country’s laws,” he said.

The CEO said separate entities are necessary in regulated sectors such as space and defence to meet national security, export control, licensing, and customer confidentiality requirements.

“Having one entity isn’t some extraordinary achievement in governance, and having several isn’t evidence of questionable patriotism,” he said.

He added that Pixxel plans to go public in India in a few years, when its complete corporate structure would be disclosed for public scrutiny.

Ahmed’s response follows comments by fellow Bengaluru-based spacetech startup GalaxEye, which said it consciously chose to remain headquartered in India despite considering other locations.

In a post on X, GalaxEye said its founders and investors had decided to build the business from India. It also highlighted its single-entity corporate structure, saying all its contracts and bids had been pursued through GalaxEye.

“Every contract and every bid we have applied for has come from a single entity: GalaxEye. We have kept our corporate structure simple and our governance clean,” it said.

Without naming any company, GalaxEye referred to the practice of setting up multiple entities across jurisdictions to qualify for and secure projects, saying it had chosen not to follow that approach.

“That discipline has a cost in the short term. We believe it pays back in trust, and trust is what a space company is ultimately built on,” it added.

Pixxel Expands Its Government Business

Founded by Ahmed and Kshitij Khandelwal, Pixxel develops hyperspectral imaging satellites that capture data across multiple narrow wavelength bands, revealing details on the Earth’s surface that conventional satellite imagery may miss.

Its new subsidiary, Pixxel Federal, will offer Earth observation technologies, satellite mission systems, and geospatial intelligence services to US government agencies. It also plans to establish an office near Washington, DC, to work more closely with government customers and partners.

The expansion builds on Pixxel’s existing engagements with NASA and the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), including a contract under NASA’s Commercial SmallSat Data Acquisition Programme and an NRO Strategic Commercial Enhancements contract.

In September, Pixxel raised $100 Mn in a Series C funding round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim, taking its total funding to around $195 Mn. 

In India, a Pixxel-led consortium is developing a 12-satellite Earth observation constellation under a public-private initiative with IN-SPACe.

item.title: Pronto Founder’s Provision Labs Acquires Hardware Startup Basilisk Industries
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Pronto founder Anjali Sardana’s physical AI venture Provision Labs has acquired Mumbai-based hardware startup Basilisk Industries for an undisclosed sum. …
item.content:encoded:
Pronto founder Anjali Sardana’s physical AI venture Provision Labs has acquired Mumbai-based hardware startup Basilisk Industries for an undisclosed sum. 

Basilisk founder Shourya Watwani will lead Provision’s hardware efforts and work on its in-house post-processing models, Sardana said in a LinkedIn post announcing the acquisition. 

Founded by Watwani in 2023, Basilisk focused on perception technologies, which help machines interpret their surroundings. 

According to Sardana, Watwani and his team have already developed a 3D hand-tracking model, redesigned Provision’s perception hardware, and built the first version of a lightweight tactile glove to capture touch-related data. 

Provision is also expanding its engineering and research teams across San Francisco, Toronto, and Bengaluru. It is hiring for work in computer vision, perception and tactile data, environment reconstruction, and hardware. 

Building Physical AI Infrastructure

Sardana recently launched San Francisco-based Provision Labs to collect data for training and testing physical AI systems — AI designed to perform real-world tasks through robots and other machines.

The startup plans to source training data from professionals across sectors globally to help developers deploy their physical AI models. Sardana serves as CEO of both Provision and Pronto.

Provision’s launch followed scrutiny of Pronto’s household recording pilot, which involved service professionals wearing cameras while performing tasks such as cleaning, washing dishes, and folding laundry.

The use of footage captured inside customers’ homes to generate training data for physical AI and robotics systems raised questions about privacy, consent, and data storage.

Pronto maintained that customers had to opt in while booking and that the pilot covered less than 0.01% of its users. It also said the pilot complied with India’s Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act and that the footage would not be shared with third-party AI labs.

Among its competitors, Snabbit said it had conducted a one-time simulation test at a training centre with data collection startup Human Archive. Urban Company said it had never recorded inside customers’ homes and had no plans to do so.

Fintech company MobiKwik reported a consolidated net profit of ₹11.8 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 as against a net loss of ₹28.6 Cr a year earlier, supported by revenue growth and lower payment processing and lending operational costs.  

Operating revenue rose 9.4% to ₹295.7 Cr from ₹270.2 Cr in Q2 FY26.

Sequentially, net profit increased 55.4% from ₹7.6 Cr, while operating revenue grew 5.1% from ₹281.5 Cr.

The company said it recorded its highest-ever quarterly net profit and fourth consecutive profitable quarter. 

EBITDA stood at ₹22.7 Cr, compared with an EBITDA loss of ₹6.4 Cr in Q2 FY26 and a profit of ₹15.8 Cr in the June quarter.

Other income declined 22.5% YoY to ₹7.1 Cr. However, total income increased 8.4% to ₹302.8 Cr from ₹279.3 Cr.

Total expenses, including finance costs and depreciation, declined 1.8% YoY to ₹290.9 Cr from ₹296.1 Cr.

Payment processing charges, MobiKwik’s largest expense, fell 10.8% YoY to ₹119.5 Cr from ₹133.9 Cr. Lending operational expenses declined 88.1% to ₹1.5 Cr from ₹12.8 Cr.

The year-ago quarter also included an ₹11.8 Cr exceptional charge related to allegedly fraudulent merchant settlements. There was no exceptional charge in Q2 FY27.

Payments Revenue Remains Flat

MobiKwik’s gross merchandise value (GMV) for the payments vertical, including its payment gateway Zaakpay, grew 35% YoY to ₹59,677 Cr, supported by growth in consumer and merchant payments.

Consumer payments accounted for ₹46,375 Cr, or 77.7%, of overall payments GMV. Merchant payments contributed the remaining 22.3%, up from about 17% a year earlier.

However, the increase in transaction value did not translate into higher payments revenue. Revenue from the business remained largely flat at ₹208.8 Cr as against ₹208.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. 

The company attributed this to a change in transaction mix towards payments that generate lower revenue relative to their value. Its payments take rate – revenue earned as a proportion of GMV – declined to 0.35% from 0.47% a year earlier.

Despite this, direct payments costs fell 12.6% YoY to ₹129 Cr, helping gross profit rise 30% to ₹79.8 Cr. Gross margin expanded to 38.2% from 29.4%.

Lending Disbursals Pick Up

Meanwhile, revenue from MobiKwik’s financial services business, which includes its ZIP EMI credit offering, increased 41.8% YoY to ₹86.9 Cr.

The growth was supported by a 34.1% increase in lending disbursals to ₹1,082.6 Cr. Disbursals also rose 46.9% sequentially from ₹736.7 Cr, recovering from a temporary dip linked to technology infrastructure migration for the transfer of its lending business.

MobiKwik increased its number of major lending partners to 11 from six a year earlier. It counts partners with quarterly disbursals exceeding ₹5 Cr as major lenders.

The company said 21% of disbursals came through its distribution model, while the remaining 79% were under its first-loss default guarantee (FLDG) model, through which it shares credit risk with lending partners and manages loan origination, servicing, and collections.

Lending-related expenses, comprising lending operational and financial guarantee expenses, declined 16.4% YoY to ₹29.8 Cr. The company attributed the reduction to improved credit quality.

Consequently, financial services gross profit more than doubled to ₹57.1 Cr from ₹25.6 Cr, while gross margin expanded to 65.7% from 41.8%.

Higher Margins Offset Costs

While both businesses improved gross margins, MobiKwik’s fixed costs rose 18.3% YoY to ₹121.2 Cr. Employee benefit expenses increased 59% to ₹56.2 Cr.

The company attributed higher employee costs to scaling its merchant business and expanding into new business areas.

Overall, the results highlight the gap between MobiKwik’s payments transaction growth and revenue, while financial services delivered stronger revenue growth. Lower direct costs across both businesses helped offset higher fixed costs and improve profitability.

“We have crossed the ₹1,000 Cr milestone in lending disbursals and clocked 150% year-on-year revenue growth in merchant payments, highlighting the growing scale of our business,” cofounder, MD, and CEO Bipin Preet Singh said.

He added that the company expects operating leverage to improve with greater AI adoption, alongside continued cost optimisation and operating efficiencies.

Shares of MobiKwik ended today’s trading session 5.57% higher at ₹225.70 apiece on the BSE.

SaaS company Capillary Technologies reported a consolidated net profit of ₹21.9 Cr in the September quarter of FY27, up over 75X from ₹28.8 Lakh in the year-ago period. The company had posted a consolidated net loss of ₹9.6 Cr in the previous quarter.

Operating revenue rose 51.3% YoY and 5.7% QoQ  to ₹271.4 Cr. Other income also almost tripled YoY to ₹6.1 Cr, taking the company’s total income for the quarter to ₹277.4 Cr.

Meanwhile, total expenses jumped 41.8% YoY to ₹257.5 Cr during the quarter. Employee benefit expenses were the biggest cost item at ₹134.1 Cr, up 51% YoY. Software and server charges came in at ₹42 Cr. Capillary booked no fresh charge in Q2. 

Capillary posted a pre-tax profit of ₹19.9 Cr against a marginal pre-tax loss in Q2 FY26. A ₹2 Cr net tax credit lifted its net profit above pre-tax earnings.

EBITDA stood at ₹45.5 Cr, more than double the ₹20.8 Cr a year ago but down about 1% from ₹46.0 Cr in Q1.

Capillary provides cloud-based customer engagement and loyalty software, helping businesses manage customer relationships and rewards programmes.

Banking authorities have frozen beneficiary accounts holding about ₹4.7 Cr (€0.43 Mn) since the end of June, and the company has filed a claim under its crime insurance policy. The independent forensic investigation has concluded without any adverse findings.

For the first half of FY27, Capillary reported revenue of ₹528 Cr, up 47% YoY from ₹359.2 Cr. Net profit for the six months stood at ₹12.4 Cr, compared to ₹1 Cr in H1 FY26.

On the operational front, the company also dissolved its Shanghai subsidiary on September 14.

The company said it is on track for its earlier FY27 guidance of ₹1,065 Cr revenue and ₹172 Cr in adjusted EBITDA.

Shares of Capillary ended today’s trading session 0.47% lower at ₹501.10 apiece on the BSE.

item.content:encoded:
Update | November 2, 15:41 IST

Shares of Delhivery ended today’s trading session 5.8% higher at ₹408.75 apiece on the BSE. The company’s market capitalisation stood at ₹30,636.7 Cr ($3.2 Bn).

Original | November 2, 12:58 IST

Shares of Delhivery jumped 9.7% to an intraday high of ₹423.35 on the BSE after the logistics company reported a consolidated net profit of ₹40.6 Cr in Q2 FY27, against a net loss of ₹50.5 Cr a year earlier.

The stock later pared some gains to trade 7.6% higher at ₹415.40 apiece at 12:12 IST. The company’s market capitalisation stood at ₹31,135.2 Cr (about $3.3 Bn) at the time.

Brokerage firm Equirus Securities upgraded Delhivery to ‘Long’ from ‘Reduce’, with a target price of ₹505. This implies an upside of 30.8% from the stock’s previous closing price of ₹386.

Equirus expects Delhivery’s revenue, EBITDA, and express parcel volumes to grow at compound annual growth rates of 21%, 39%, and 22%, respectively, between FY26 and FY29, driven by market share gains, improving part truckload (PTL) margins, and operating leverage.

The brokerage estimates revenue of ₹12,963.3 Cr in FY27 and ₹15,107.3 Cr in FY28, with net profit of ₹381.4 Cr and ₹694.5 Cr, respectively.

Revenue Growth Outpaces Expenses

Delhivery’s consolidated operating revenue rose 19.8% to ₹3,066.4 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹2,559.3 Cr a year earlier. Sequentially, revenue increased 4.6% from ₹2,930.7 Cr.

Including other income of ₹66.6 Cr, total income stood at ₹3,133 Cr, compared with ₹2,651.5 Cr in Q2 FY26.

Total expenses increased 14.2% to ₹3,093 Cr from ₹2,708.1 Cr. Freight, handling, and servicing costs, its largest expense head, rose 19.1% to ₹2,195.1 Cr.

The company posted a pre-tax profit of ₹39 Cr against a loss of ₹53.2 Cr a year earlier. A net tax credit of ₹1.6 Cr took its consolidated net profit to ₹40.6 Cr.

However, Delhivery’s acquisition of Ecom Express affected the comparison. Excluding the acquisition impact, the company said its net profit in Q2 FY26 and Q1 FY27 would have stood at ₹59 Cr and ₹62 Cr, respectively.

Express Parcel Volumes Rise

Delhivery’s express parcel volumes rose 32.1% YoY to 325 Mn shipments, driven by market share gains and customer demand. Equirus said growth exceeded its FY27 guidance of 20-30%.

PTL volumes increased 14.2% to 5.45 Lakh metric tonnes, while revenue grew 23.2% on higher volumes and yields. Equirus attributed less than 30% of the yield increase to inflation-linked pricing revisions.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 48% YoY to ₹123 Cr, with margins improving to 4% from 3.3%.

Supported by pricing revisions and higher network utilisation, Delhivery expects express parcel service EBITDA margins to reach 16-18% and PTL margins to exceed 15% by FY27-end. Overall transportation margins are expected to expand 130-150 basis points during FY27.

Delhivery Local Revenue Run Rate Doubles To ₹200 Cr

Delhivery is expanding its intra-city, international, and financial services businesses. Delhivery Local operates across Delhi NCR, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Pune, and Chennai. Its annualised revenue run rate doubled sequentially to around ₹200 Cr in Q2 FY27.

The company raised the platform’s FY27 exit run rate target to ₹280 Cr from ₹250 Cr, targeting ₹800-1,000 Cr in annualised revenue within two years.

Its board also approved an equity investment of up to ₹36 Cr in wholly owned subsidiary Delhivery Fintech Distribution, supporting financial product distribution across its vendor network and co-lending partnerships.

Delhivery said AI automation cut customer support and proof-of-delivery validation costs by over 50% without affecting quality. It has begun manufacturing customised autonomous mobile robots through Delhivery Labs and plans to deploy 100 self-developed autonomous pallet transportation vehicles by Q4 FY27.

October volumes exceeded the company’s initial expectations.

item.title: Can Indrajaal Build A ₹100 Cr Business Protecting India’s Skies?
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: In September 2019, a swarm of low-cost drones launched by Houthi rebels struck Saudi Aramco’s oil processing facilities, knocking out…
item.content:encoded:
In September 2019, a swarm of low-cost drones launched by Houthi rebels struck Saudi Aramco’s oil processing facilities, knocking out nearly half of Saudi Arabia’s oil production. The attack sent shockwaves across the world, exposing how inexpensive flying machines could bring critical infrastructure to a standstill.

Back home, the founder of Indrajaal, Kiran Raju, was closely observing everything, including a rise in drone incursions along India’s borders. He foresaw that Indian security agencies would soon need technology to detect hostile drones and stop them before they could launch an attack.

Indrajaal is looking to tackle this growing threat through its AI-powered counter-drone technology designed to detect, track and neutralise hostile drones, protecting military installations and critical infrastructure from aerial threats. Founded in 2020, the defence tech startup is developing an advanced, AI-powered counter-drone systems that combine proprietary hardware, computer vision and machine learning. It has so far raised about $5.5 Mn in external funding from the likes of India Accelerator and Finvolve. 

The founder’s journey into autonomous robotics began long before Indrajaal. After studying at Carnegie Mellon University, he founded Grene Robotics in 2006 to develop autonomous technologies for defence applications. As drones became cheaper and more advanced, he spun off Indrajaal from Grene Robotics to develop systems capable of detecting and countering aerial threats.

Inside Indrajaal’s Defence Tech Capabilities 

Traditional counter-drone systems typically rely on standalone technologies to jam or shoot down hostile drones. However, this approach becomes less effective when friendly and hostile drones operate in the same airspace.

Indrajaal addresses this limitation through SkyOS, its AI-powered platform that brings together multiple detection and defence systems.

SkyOS uses real-time data from radars, radio-frequency sensors and cameras to detect, track and identify aerial threats. Based on this information, it can recommend or automatically execute countermeasures.

The startup also offers an AI-powered mobile counter-drone vehicle, Ranger, designed to detect and neutralise threats while on the move. Once a hostile drone is identified, the system can jam its signals, use Repulsor to interfere with its navigation or deploy SkyCop, an autonomous interceptor drone.

All these products operate within Indrajaal’s integrated defence architecture, allowing the company to offer different solutions for different security requirements.

Indrajaal Spreads Its Wings

The startup operates in India’s growing defence tech sector, which is projected to become a $19 Bn market opportunity by 2030. Government incentives, homegrown innovation and the push for self-reliance in defence are driving this growth.

The startup has already deployed its systems at critical installations belonging to the Indian Army, Indian Navy and agencies under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Indrajaal makes money through these deployments, supplying customers with a combination of hardware, software, installation and long-term maintenance services tailored to their security requirements.

Here’s how its growth trajectory looks like:

  • Revenue grew from around ₹34 Cr in FY25 to ₹100 Cr in FY26, with a target of ₹300 Cr in FY27
  • Plans to raise ₹420 Cr in its upcoming Series A round
  • Looking to ramp up manufacturing capacity, strengthen R&D and enter markets across the Middle East and Europe
  • Plans to expand its workforce from around 100 to nearly 160 employees over the coming year
  • Aims to develop a broader autonomous airspace ecosystem supporting civilian drone corridors and autonomous aerial transport

Inc42 Take: Government Contracts Could Be Indrajaal’s Achilles’ Heel

Indrajaal appears to have found its financial footing in the market with its novel tech stack. But, the startup is heavily tied to government contracts, which carry long validation windows and multi-year sales cycles. This could expose the startup to high working-capital strain.

On top of this, Indrajaal operates on a customised business model, which can strain gross margins and make scaling unit economics significantly harder. There are also supply chain risks and cost inflation that can quickly erode profitability and margins.

Meanwhile, competition also shows no signs of slowing down. As more global giants enter the fray, the startup will be up against players with deeper pockets and mature distribution channels. Domestically, too, rapid defence indigenisation has encouraged rivals to launch rival counter-drone systems, threatening pricing power.

While Indrajaal has built a battle-tested defence business, sustaining its ambitious financial trajectory will require transitioning beyond defence contracts to roping in private enterprises and successfully executing its international expansion across high-budget defence markets.

item.title: UPI Transactions Rise 5.8% MoM To Record 25.47 Bn In October
item.dc:creator: Anjali Jain
item.description: UPI transaction volume rose 5.8% MoM to a record 25.47 Bn in October from 24.07 Bn in September, according to…
item.content:encoded:
UPI transaction volume rose 5.8% MoM to a record 25.47 Bn in October from 24.07 Bn in September, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).

The value of transactions processed through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) increased 7.4% MoM to a record ₹31.53 Lakh Cr from ₹29.37 Lakh Cr in the previous month.

On a YoY basis, transaction volume grew 23%, while transaction value rose 16%.

October marked the first month in which UPI processed more than 25 Bn transactions and payments worth over ₹30 Lakh Cr. Average daily transaction value also crossed ₹1 Lakh Cr for the first time.

UPI processed an average of 822 Mn transactions a day in October, up from 802 Mn in September. Average daily transaction value increased to ₹1,01,707 Cr from ₹97,913 Cr.

The daily averages provide a clearer comparison of payment activity because October had 31 days against September’s 30. Based on NPCI’s figures, average daily volume increased 2.5% MoM, while average daily value rose 3.9%.

The increase coincided with the festive season. October’s growth followed a marginal decline in September, when transaction volume fell 1.8% MoM and transaction value dropped 1.5%.

Merchant Charges On Horizon

The latest figures come ahead of the proposed introduction of merchant discount rate (MDR) charges on select UPI payments.

The NPCI deferred the rollout, originally scheduled for October 15, until after Diwali, saying the new implementation date would be notified separately.

MDR is the fee merchants pay banks and payment companies to process digital transactions. Under the revised framework, eligible person-to-merchant (P2M) payments above ₹2,000 will attract a 0.4% charge, capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 and above. Person-to-person (P2P) payments will remain free of MDR.

The revised structure would create a revenue stream for banks and payment service providers processing eligible transactions, potentially improving monetisation across the UPI ecosystem. However, merchant bodies have raised concerns over the additional payment acceptance costs and sought relief ahead of the rollout.

item.title: CBI Extradites Mahadev Betting App Promoter Sourabh Chandrakar From Oman
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has extradited Sourabh Chandrakar, a promoter of the Mahadev Online Book betting platform, from…
item.content:encoded:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has extradited Sourabh Chandrakar, a promoter of the Mahadev Online Book betting platform, from Oman to India.

A specially deputed CBI team brought Chandrakar back yesterday following coordination between Indian agencies and Omani authorities, the agency said in a statement.

He is expected to be produced before a CBI Special Court in Raipur today after a medical examination and completion of transit remand formalities.

Chandrakar faces two CBI cases in which chargesheets have been filed, besides a money laundering case registered by the Enforcement Directorate (ED), in which a prosecution complaint has been filed.

The Royal Oman Police located and detained him following an Interpol Red Corner Notice. The CBI and ED subsequently submitted formal extradition requests, supported by evidence gathered against him.

The process was coordinated through Indian government agencies and Interpol’s National Central Bureau, with support from Omani authorities. The CBI described his extradition as a significant step in bringing back fugitives accused of running transnational criminal operations targeting Indian citizens.

How The Network Operated 

The CBI took up the Mahadev Online Book cases at the Chhattisgarh government’s request.

According to investigators, the platform operated from outside India through a network of franchised panels and branches that enrolled users and facilitated illegal betting on cricket, football, card games, and other events.

The CBI alleged that betting proceeds were routed through mule bank accounts, layered across multiple transactions, and transferred overseas through hawala channels. Part of the money was allegedly paid to public servants as protection money to allow the syndicate to operate without hindrance. 

ED’s Overseas Asset Trail

The ED has estimated the proceeds of crime in the Mahadev betting app case at around ₹6,000 Cr. Its investigation has also examined alleged links to senior politicians and bureaucrats in Chhattisgarh.

In March, the agency provisionally attached 20 properties with an estimated market value of nearly ₹1,700 Cr under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).

These included 18 properties in Dubai, comprising villas and apartments in Burj Khalifa, Dubai Hills Estate, Business Bay, and SLS Hotel & Residences, besides two properties in New Delhi.

The ED alleged that the properties were acquired using illegal betting proceeds and held through entities controlled by Chandrakar and his associates, including Vikas Chhaparia, Rohit Gulati, Atul Arora, and Surendra Bagri.

According to the agency, Mahadev Online Book facilitated betting through platforms and domain names such as Tiger Exchange, Gold365, and Laser247. Chandrakar and fellow promoter Ravi Uppal allegedly controlled the franchise network from Dubai.

The promoters allegedly retained 70-75% of the betting profits, with the remainder distributed among panel operators. Investigators said the proceeds were moved through mule and dummy bank accounts, hawala channels, cryptocurrency transactions, and layered financial structures before being invested in assets in India and the UAE.

In its March 25 statement, the ED put the cumulative value of assets attached, seized, or frozen at around ₹4,336 Cr. At that point, it had searched more than 175 locations, arrested 13 people, and filed five prosecution complaints against 74 accused.

The agency also said it had filed applications under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018, against Chandrakar, Uppal, Anil Agrawal alias Atul Agrawal, and Shubham Soni, seeking their declaration as fugitive economic offenders and confiscation of their properties.

The wider investigation has also examined alleged links involving EaseMyTrip cofounder Nishant Pitti and former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel. Both have denied wrongdoing.

Indian VCs And The Deeptech Dilemma

Skyroot has proved that homegrown startups can build rockets, but the bigger challenge may lie in funding them. A recent viral critique of Indian venture capitalists has reignited the debate over deeptech funding gaps, risk appetite of investors and slow diligence. 

Founder Grievances: For many early stage founders, deeptech funding in India remains plagued by prolonged due diligence, demands for commercial traction before validation and an over-reliance on founder pedigree. Their criticism is aimed at the current system, which may be underwriting very little genuine technological risk and backing a handful of startups.

Concentration Problem: Data adds further nuance to the debate. Deeptech funding surged 176% YoY in Q3 2026, but the deal count barely moved. This is because most of the capital was heavily concentrated among a few players and that too in Bengaluru. The pattern suggests that the capital is largely flowing to technically validated companies, while early stage founders pursuing unproven scientific experiments still struggle to secure their first cheque.

Why Investors Hesitate? Indian VCs have historically been hesitant towards deeptech bets due to the sector’s long gestation cycles, uncertain exits, specialised diligence and substantial follow-on capital. Venture funds also operate under pressure from limited partners to mint returns and liquidity within defined timelines. As a result, most VCs hesitate to underwrite these uncertain scientific bets.

Changing Ecosystem: However, the picture is not entirely bleak. Founder-led vehicles and specialist funds are expanding and raising big bucks for moonshots. Government initiatives, like the ₹1 Lakh Cr RDI Fund, are also creating more optimism around deeptech. But capital alone will not solve the problem as local frontier ventures still need stronger follow-on funding, patient limited partners and the corporate willing to buy early products.

Indian founders have proved that they can build rockets, but can VCs now step in and show that they can finance these moonshot bets? Let’s find out…

From The Editor’s Desk

Weekly Funding Rundown 

  • Indian startups cumulatively raised $130.2 Mn last week, down 29% from $184 Mn in the preceding week. However, deal count zoomed 88% week-on-week to 32. Cent and Simplismart took the biggest cheques home at $15 Mn and $14 Mn, respectively.
  • Ecommerce emerged as the most funded sector last week, bagging $33 Mn across nine deals. Following suit were AI ventures, which bagged $30 Mn across five deals. 
  • On the investor front, Blume Ventures and Antler emerged as the most active investors last week and backed three startups each.

E2W Sales In October

  • Electric two-wheeler registrations grew a marginal 2.9% month-on-month to 2.1 Lakh units in October. Sales also rose 48% YoY from 1.4 Lakh units a year earlier. 
  • Legacy giants TVS Motor and Hero MotoCorp recorded gains and improved their market share to 27.2% and 13.4%, respectively. However, Bajaj Auto reported a decline in sales in October, which led to its market share falling to 21.7% from 23.4% in September.
  • Growth also tapered off for new-age EV makers in October. Ather’s registrations declined 1.8% to 30,380 units from 30,942 units in September, while its market share slipped to 14.2%. Ola Electric’s sales also tanked 13.7% MoM to 11,614 units last month. 

Kickback Allegations At Flipkart

  • Walmart has launched a probe into allegations that employees at the ecommerce giant received over ₹150 Cr in kickbacks from vendors. The charges have been directed against employees in Flipkart’s smartphones and luggage and travel accessories divisions.
  • The complaints allege the certain employees accepted payments and favours from vendors in exchange for preferential treatment on the ecommerce platform, including greater visibility that helped drive sales.
  • This is Walmart’s third investigation into alleged financial misconduct at Flipkart in the past three years. A previous probe resulted in three dismissals two-and-a-half years ago, while another investigation found wrongdoing by an employee barely six months ago.

eMudhra & Accountability

  • The cybersecurity firm came under fire last month after researchers discovered that its private keys were weak and could be recovered in under a second. The row saw eMudhra exit the global TLS certificate business altogether. 
  • The episode demonstrates that global browser makers, rather than local regulators, became the first line of accountability for eMudhra. This raises a governance question for India: who investigates and prevents a similar failure domestically?
  • Experts now flag that eMudhra’s exit means that Indian websites may increasingly depend on foreign certificate authorities for trust. This could affect India’s digital sovereignty and its ability to build a domestic public-key infrastructure ecosystem.

Bullish Week For Startup Stocks

  • Of the 69 new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 40 gained between 0.2% and 26.8%, last week. However, the remaining 29 declined by up to 22.3%. Startup stocks largely saw gains as quarterly earnings drove sharp moves in individual counters. 
  • Ather Energy and Zetwerk emerged as the biggest gainers, while shares of CarTrade and AceVector shed the most. The combined market-cap of these 69 stocks jumped to $160.9 Bn at the end of last week, up 5.7% from $152.3 Bn in the week-ago period.
  • Going forward, investors will track the upcoming US midterm elections, Brent crude oil prices, geopolitical developments and quarterly earnings for market cues this week.

upliance.ai Eyes $4 Mn

  • The D2C home appliance maker in advanced talks to raise $3 Mn to $4 Mn in its Series A round. The fundraise will likely see participation from a fresh investor, while existing backers, including Khosla Ventures, will also double down.
  • Founded in 2021, upliance.ai sells AI-powered kitchen appliances like food processors and air fryers. The D2C brand had last raised ₹34 Cr in a seed round led by Khosla Ventures in 2024 at a valuation of ₹143 Cr.
  • The development comes amid growing activity in India’s smart kitchen appliances market, which is being driven by growing demand for automated products and rising disposable incomes. The space is projected to become a $3 Bn opportunity by 2032.

Inc42 Markets

Inc42 Startup Spotlight

How D-Propulse Is Rethinking Jet Engines

India has pursued indigenous jet-engine capability for decades now, but to no avail. This has created heavy dependence on overseas vendors and costly testing. D-Propulse is betting on a new technology to build lighter, cheaper propulsion for high-speed drones and missiles.

The RDE Approach: Founded in 2025, D-Propulse is developing rotating detonation engines (RDEs), which use supersonic detonation waves to generate thrust. It has already tested a 5 kN air-breathing RDE that is currently at technology readiness level-5. The startup claims its engine will be 15-25% more efficient and at least 60% less expensive than conventional ramjets.

Eye On The Prize: To scale its ambitions, the startup is also building a 5,000+ sq ft combustor test facility at IIT Madras, with air mass flow capacity of around 10 kg/sec and an in-house HPC cluster. It is also exploring infrastructure rental as an early revenue stream while its jet engine business takes shape.

Building For Defence: D-Propulse is targeting the Indian Armed Forces as its intended first customers. It now plans to conduct flight tests between June and December 2027 and limited series production by the end of 2028. The pre-revenue startup also plans to raise a Series A round by early next year.

With the global RDE opportunity projected to surpass $2.4 Bn by 2030, can D-Propulse build commercially viable jet engines for India?

item.title: Two Point O Bags $10 Mn To Bridge The Financing Gap In Clean Energy
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: India’s clean energy transition is attracting significant capital, but much of it is flowing into utility-scale projects. Smaller installations across…
item.content:encoded:
India’s clean energy transition is attracting significant capital, but much of it is flowing into utility-scale projects. Smaller installations across factories, commercial buildings and industrial facilities continue to face a financing gap, even when the technology is commercially viable and can help businesses lower operating costs.

Two Point O Capital wants to channel capital into this underserved segment by bringing financing, technology and project execution under one platform.

To fuel its ambition, the startup has now raised $10 Mn (nearly ₹95 Cr) in its Series A round led by Transition Venture Capital (TVC). The round also saw participation from existing backer Omnivore and angel investors Chiranjeev Singh Saluja and Sudhir M Reddy.

The startup plans to utilise a major chunk of the fresh proceeds towards financing the deployment of clean energy assets for its commercial and industrial (C&I) customers. The capital will also be utilised to strengthen the startup’s tech stack and ramp up hiring.

The latest round comes two years after Two Point O raised over $6 Mn, via a mix of equity and debt, in 2024 .

“There was a lot of capital that was getting pumped into utility-scale, grid-scale projects. But there wasn’t enough capital inflows into the distributed or decentralised energy projects, to put it simply, for industries and buildings,” cofounder and CEO Karan Bhutani told Inc42.

Founded in 2024 by Bhutani, Archit Mehrotra, Manya Ranjan and Shashidhar Reddy, Two Point O provides financing, turnkey solutions and equipment leasing across areas such as rooftop solar, battery energy storage systems (BESS) and wastewater treatment. Unlike traditional banks and NBFCs, the startup claims to be focused on smaller-scale projects.

 

Building A Full-Stack Clean Energy Platform

Two Point O positions itself as a full-stack clean energy enablement platform for commercial and industrial (C&I) customers. Its offerings span four asset classes:

  • Rooftop Solar: Distributed solar installations for commercial and industrial facilities
  • BESS: Solutions to optimise energy consumption and manage peak demand
  • Energy Efficiency: Upgrades across heating, cooling and air compressors
  • Wastewater treatment: Projects to improve water treatment and resource utilisation

The startup offers multiple financing structures. It operates a wholly-owned NBFC subsidiary, which handles loan disbursals, while a separate operating entity caters to lease and service-based requirements.

Bhutani also claims that the startup has built a proprietary underwriting engine that uses technology to assess a project’s technical specifications, performance and credit profiles. This allows Two Point O to dish out a techno-commercial proposal for a client within 24 to 48 hours, he added.

Two Point O also monitors assets after deployment. Bhutani said that all deployed assets are IoT-enabled, with real-time data used for preventive maintenance, performance optimisation and verification.

Notably, the startup does not directly undertake installation and maintenance. Instead, it relies on original equipment manufacturers as well as engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) partners for execution, and oversees them through technology and contracts. Bhutani said that this “light-touch” model gives the startup the ability to scale its operations.

Inside Two Point O’s Cross-Selling Model

India’s clean tech market, as per IMARC Group, could become a $95 Bn opportunity by 2034. Two Point O is eyeing a much smaller piece of this market as it operates at the intersection of lending tech and B2B clean energy enablement segments. 

To carve a niche in the space, Two Point O has so far focused on roping in big-ticket clients and cross-selling additional solutions to these customers. This approach, as per Bhutani, allows the startup to keep customer acquisition costs low and get more out of its users. 

So far, the startup claims to have already onboarded around 25-30 large customers, including Premier Energies, Godrej, JK Tyre, Morepen Pharma, Wipro and Phoenix Mills. Bhutani estimates that its existing customer base could generate ₹400-500 Cr in transactions over the next two to three years. The startup also noted that its assets under management (AUM) grew 1.5X sequentially in each of the last three quarters.

Not stopping there, the startup has much more in store going forward:

  • Enter the SME segment and expand across India
  • Build an AUM of $75 Mn to $100 Mn over the next couple of years
  • Expand into new sectors like data centres, automotives, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing and healthcare

Inc42 Take: Can Two Point O Scale Its Multi-Asset Model?

Two Point O is addressing a financing gap in distributed clean energy by combining capital, technology and project execution. What works for the startup is its multi-asset model, which could help deepen relationships with existing customers and generate repeat business.

However, scaling across asset classes will require strong underwriting, consistent asset performance and effective oversight of operating partners. The planned SME expansion also brings additional challenges around technology risks, regulations and credit assessment.

The startup’s ability to turn its customer base and growing AUM into sustained revenue and profitability remains to be seen, particularly as it expands its portfolio and deployment commitments.

item.content:encoded:
Dalal Street emerged as a founder’s paradise in 2025, with 18 Indian startups listing on the bourses and collectively mopping up a record ₹41,248 Cr from the public markets.

The surge was driven by a combination of macroeconomic tailwinds and regulatory support. While robust GDP growth projections helped revive investor appetite, SEBI’s reforms played a key role. Measures such as simplified DRHP filings reduced red tape, while more flexible ESOP rules allowed founders to retain meaningful ownership.

Retail investors also fuelled the frenzy as demat accounts crossed the 20 Cr mark. The OFS component dominated public issues last year, providing liquidity to the early backers of the new-age tech companies. Post-listing performance also followed the usual curve, with investors rewarding companies that prioritised profits, sustainable growth and governance over hype. 

“⁠Besides the readiness that startups showed in their unit economics, there is also an increase in the founders committing to their businesses for next couple of decades and grow their businesses by adding adjacent profit pools – something that the public markets reward handsomely,” said Ashish Kumar, cofounder and general partner at Fundamentum Partnership.

Building on the momentum, seventeen new-age tech companies have already made their D-Street debut so far this year. Of these, ESDS Software Solution, Klassroom, RentoMojo, SEDEMAC, Kissht, LEAP India and Shiprocket made a bumper debut on the bourses. 

Nevertheless, the IPO pipeline remains strong. Twenty five startups have already filed their DRHPs with SEBI, while over 25 are in various stages of finalising their IPO plans. Unicorns like OYO and Razorpay alone could raise nearly ₹20,000 Cr in 2026, making it one of the biggest years for startup IPOs.

However, recalibration is likely to define 2026 as investors are expected to prioritise strong fundamentals, profitability and low cash burn when backing new-age tech companies. 

“IPO-bound startups in 2026 will be increasingly defined by their ability to demonstrate predictable cash flows, sustainable unit economics, and operational discipline rather than headline growth alone. Public market investors will place greater emphasis on governance, capital efficiency and long-term value creation, favouring companies that balance scale with financial prudence,” Orios Venture Partners’ managing partner Rehan Yar Khan told Inc42.

There are other challenges as well. Average retail subscription levels are moderating, while foreign institutional investors (FIIs) are pulling back in droves, reflecting caution amid geopolitical tensions and muted secondary market performance. The ongoing conflict in West Asia has further complicated the situation.

Yet, the overall outlook remains bullish for new-age tech IPOs. Maturing business models, deeper domestic capital pools and an evolving regulatory framework favouring transparency position India as a leading startup IPO hub.
